STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r3.claim: The sūrah takes its name from Abraham’s episode and prayer, which asks security for Makkah, protection from idolatry for himself and his children, and prosperity for his progeny.
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r3.anchor: the security of Makkah, protection from idolatry for himself and his children, prosperity for his progeny

STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r4.claim: Abraham also prayed for forgiveness for his parents and all believers on the Last Day.
STUDYQURAN:14:intro/r4.anchor: forgiveness for his parents and all believers on the Last Day.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Abraham's prayers concern Makkah and his children settled there, showing Quraysh that their lives oppose his hopes while Muhammad and his followers fulfill them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The purpose is to make evident to the Quraysh that the whole life that they are leading is totally against the supplications and desires of Abraham (sws).

SAMIN-DURR:14:40/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:40/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:14:40/r1.claim: ومن ذريتي coordinates with the first object of اجعلني: make some of my descendants establish prayer; it describes an omitted بعضا.
SAMIN-DURR:14:40/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { ومن ذريتي }: عطف على المفعول الأول ل " اجعلني " ، أي: واجعل بعض ذريتي مقيم الصلاة.

SAMIN-DURR:14:40/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:14:40/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة وورش
SAMIN-DURR:14:40/r2.claim: Abu Amr, Hamza, and Warsh retain the final yāʾ in connected recitation but drop it at pause; al-Bazzi retains it in both, while others drop it in both, with reports of retention at pause too.
SAMIN-DURR:14:40/r2.anchor: قوله: { وتقبل دعآء } قرأ أو عمرو وحمزة وورش بإثبات الياء وصلا وحذفها وقفا

ZAJJAJ:v3p165/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p165/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p165/r1.claim: Abraham asks God to make some of his descendants people who establish prayer.
ZAJJAJ:v3p165/r1.anchor: أي واجعل من ذريتي من يقيم الصلاة.

ZAJJAJ:v3p165/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p165/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p165/r2.claim: At pause دعائي is read without the final yāʾ; in connected speech one may omit it, retain it (the best form), or give it sukūn or fatḥa.
ZAJJAJ:v3p165/r2.anchor: في دعائي، إذا وقفت، فإذا وصلت فأنت بالخيار إن شئت

ASAD-NOTES:14:39/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:39/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:39/r2.claim: Abraham asks God to keep him and some of his descendants constant in prayer.
ASAD-NOTES:14:39/r2.anchor: cause me and [some] of my offspring to remain constant in prayer

ASAD-NOTES:14:39#n54/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:39#n54/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:39#n54/r1.claim: “Establish prayer” is metonymic for remaining utterly devoted to God.
ASAD-NOTES:14:39#n54/r1.anchor: metonymically, "to remain utterly devoted to Thee"

ASAD-NOTES:14:39#n54/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:14:39#n54/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:14:39#n54/r2.claim: The phrase “some of my offspring” alludes to 2:124: Abraham understands that some descendants will be evildoers, so lineage cannot make anyone a chosen person. This applies to Israelite and Ishmaelite branches, including Quraysh and unrighteous descendants of Muhammad.
ASAD-NOTES:14:39#n54/r2.anchor: is obviously an allusion to 2:124, where God says in answer to Abraham's question about his descendants

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Abraham asks his descendants to carry on the prayer-centred purpose for which he built the House.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: he has supplicated for his progeny to fully adhere to the purpose

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The phrase “from my progeny” shows that only Ishmael, not all Abraham's descendants, was settled there.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The expression “from my progeny” aptly tells us that only one part of his progeny

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Islahi counts Rabbi or Rabbana seven times and says the apparent repetition is essential to supplication, which repeatedly humbles itself and seeks God's attention.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This apparently seems a repetition. Yet this is a feature of a supplication; in fact, it is essential.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Using Rabbi presents as grounds for the plea a favour of God the supplicant has personally experienced.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: he wants to include as recommendation for his supplication the favour of God he has experienced.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Using Rabbana presents as grounds for the plea a favour witnessed by all God's creatures.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: he wants to include as recommendation for his supplication

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The prayer is retold to Quraysh so they remember why they were settled in the barren valley, recognize Abraham's prayer as the source of their blessings, and see that they wrongly credit their alleged deities.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: this supplication has been narrated to the Quraysh so that they recall the reason for being settled in this barren stretch of land

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p33#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p33#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة وهبيرة عن حفص عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p33#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Hamza, and Hubayra from Hafs from Asim retain yāʾ in duʿāʾī in connected reading; al-Bazzi retains it in both connection and pause, while Qunbul hints at it in connection and pauses without it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p33#2/r1.anchor: (وتقبل دعائي ربنا) بياء في الوصل وقال البزي عن ابن كثير

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p33#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p33#2/r2.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p33#2/r2.claim: The remaining readers omit the yāʾ; the source specifies al-Kisai and Ibn Amir among those omitting it in both connection and pause.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p33#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p33#2/r3.speaker: نافع
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p33#2/r3.claim: Al-Asmaʿi reports hearing Nafi connect with yāʾ, while other transmitters report that Nafi omitted it in both connection and pause.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p33#2/r3.anchor: روى نصر بن علي عن الأصمعي قال: سمعت نافعا يقرأ: (وتقبل دعائي ربنا) بياء في الوصل

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p33#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p33#2/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p33#2/r4.claim: Keeping yāʾ at Ibn Kathir's pause and connection, and in Asim's connected reading, follows the regular analogy; Qunbul's hinted yāʾ is also permissible because the kasra signals it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p33#2/r4.anchor: أما وقف ابن كثير ووصله بياء فهو القياس، وأما وصل عاصم: (وتقبل دعائي) بياء فقياس

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p33#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p33#2/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p33#2/r5.claim: Deletion is acceptable at verse endings as in poetic rhyme, and is more apt at pause than in connection because pause commonly changes the final sound; al-Aʿsha's lines illustrate omission.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p33#2/r5.anchor: لأن الفواصل وما أشبه الفواصل من الكلام التام يحسن الحذف فيه، كما يحسن في القوافي

IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r5.speaker: ابن كثير، حمزة، أبو عمرو، حفص عن عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r5.claim: These readings retain yāʾ in دعاء in connected recitation; al-Bazzī reports Ibn Kathīr retaining it in both connection and pause.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r5.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وحمزة وأبو عمرو وحفص عن عاصم فى رواية هبيرة عن حفص ﴿ وتقبل دعاء ﴾ بياء فى الوصل

IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r6.speaker: ابن كثير عن البزي، نافع عن الأصمعي، ورش
IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r6.claim: Al-Bazzī reports yāʾ from Ibn Kathīr in both positions; al-Aṣmaʿī and Warsh report it from Nāfiʿ in connection, unlike other Nāfiʿ routes.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r6.anchor: وقال البزى عن ابن كثير يصل ويقف بياء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r7.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r7.speaker: عاصم عن أبي عمارة، قنبل عن ابن كثير، نافع عن غير الأصمعي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r7.claim: Abū ʿUmāra reports no yāʾ from ʿĀṣim in either position; Qunbul reports Ibn Kathīr hinting at it in connection but stopping on alif; other Nāfiʿ routes omit it.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r7.anchor: وروى أبو عمارة عن أبي حفص عن أبي عمر عن عاصم ﴿ وتقبل دعاء ﴾ بغير ياء فى وصل ووقف

IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r8.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r8.speaker: الكسائي، ابن عامر، عاصم عن أبي بكر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r8.claim: Al-Kisāʾī, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Abū Bakr’s transmission from ʿĀṣim omit yāʾ in connection and pause.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p362/r8.anchor: وقرأ الكسائى وابن عامر وعاصم فى رواية أبى بكر بغير ياء فى وصل ولا وقف

NASHR:v2p300/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p300/r10.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو وحمزة وورش ويعقوب والبزي وقنبل
NASHR:v2p300/r10.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza, and Warsh retain the extra yāʾ in connection; Yaʿqūb and al-Bazzī do so in both states, while Qunbul varies between connection and pause.
NASHR:v2p300/r10.anchor: وتقبل دعاء أثبتها وصلا أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو وحمزة وورش

NASHR:v2p460/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p460/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p460/r5.claim: Supplication should begin and end with praise of God, with blessings on the Prophet afterward; Abraham’s prayer models praise before asking, moving from God’s knowledge and gifts to the request that he and his descendants establish prayer.
NASHR:v2p460/r5.anchor: الثناء على الله تعالى أولا وآخرا أي قبل الدعاء

NASHR:v1p344/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p344/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p344/r1.claim: For the discussed case, lengthening is possible under the general rule, but shortening is more likely because both hamzat al-waṣl and the initial position are incidental and should not determine length.

NASHR:v1p344/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p344/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p344/r2.claim: For Warsh, the three phrases ملة آبائي إبراهيم, فلم يزدهم دعائي إلا, and وتقبل دعاء follow his usual lengthening patterns by their underlying forms, disregarding incidental opening or orthographic deletion; this is the author’s analogy, learned in performance for Ibrahim’s دعاء.

QIRAAT-ER:14:40:11#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:14:40:11#1/r1.speaker: Yz
QIRAAT-ER:14:40:11#1/r1.claim: Yz explicitly pronounces the possessive first-person yāʾ in duʿāʾī, making the first-person possession overt.
QIRAAT-ER:14:40:11#1/r1.anchor: Yz, mutawatir: Explicit yāʾ al-mutakallim appended — duʿāʾī instead of duʿāʾi; makes the 1st person possessive visible

QIRAAT-ER:14:40:11#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:14:40:11#2/r1.speaker: Yz
QIRAAT-ER:14:40:11#2/r1.claim: Yz allows pausing on duʿāʾ without possessive yāʾ (“the calling”) or continuing with duʿāʾī (“my calling”), creating a waqf/waṣl interpretive difference.
QIRAAT-ER:14:40:11#2/r1.anchor: Yz, mutawatir: "Dual reading: either stopping on duʿāʾ (without possessive yāʾ — open/universal

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p449/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p449/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p449/r4.claim: Although Abraham already performs prayer, he asks to remain constant in establishing it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p449/r4.anchor: ودعاؤه بأن يجعله مقيم الصلاة وهو مقيمها، إنما يريد بذلك الديمومة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p449/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p449/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p449/r5.claim: Min is partitive because Abraham knew some descendants would disbelieve or neglect prayer despite being believers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p449/r5.anchor: ومن ذريتي، من للتبعيض، لأنه أعلم أن من ذريته من يكون كافرا، أو من يهمل إقامتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p449/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p449/r6.speaker: طلحة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p449/r6.claim: Talha and al-Aʿmash read دعاء ربنا without the yāʾ; Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr use a still yāʾ in connection, some preserve it at pause, and Warsh from Nafiʿ keeps it in connection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p449/r6.anchor: وقرأ طلحة، والأعمش: دعاء ربنا بغير ياء. وقرأ ابن كثير، وأبو عمرو: بياء ساكنة في الوصل

ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r1.claim: Muqīm al-ṣalāh means making prayer upright and sound, metaphorically like straightening a crooked stick; Abraham asks for constancy in that practice.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r1.anchor: معدلا لها فهو مجاز من أقمت العود اذا قومته وأراد بهذا الدعاء الديمومة على ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r2.claim: Some interpret the phrase as regular observance; one eminent scholar combines regularity with constancy, treating the nominal form as adding the former without assigning two metaphorical senses.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r2.anchor: وجوز بعضهم أن يكون المعنى مواظبا عليها وبعض عظماء العلماء أخذ الأمرين في تفسير ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r3.claim: Abraham uses the singular for himself although the prayer includes descendants to mark himself as their exemplar and them as his followers.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r3.anchor: للاشعار بأنه المقتدى في ذلك وذريته أتباع له

ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r4.claim: Min is partitive: Abraham asks that some of his descendants establish prayer, since he knew some would not, through unbelief or failure to pray; alternatively he inferred this from God’s practice among earlier peoples.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r4.anchor: ( ومن ) للتبعيض والعطف كما قال أبو البقاء على مفعول ( اجعل ) الاول

ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r5.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ coordinates min dhurriyyatī with the first object of ajʿal, meaning ‘and some of my descendants’ as prayer performers.

ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r6.speaker: الحواشي الشهابية
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r6.claim: The Shihāb marginalia says the prepositional phrase modifies an elided noun coordinated with the first object (‘some of my descendants’); without that estimate, the construction is awkward.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r6.anchor: وفي الحواشي الشهابية أن الجار والمجرور في الحقيقة صفة للمعطوف على ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r7.claim: The apparent sense is ‘accept this supplication’ concerning making Abraham and some descendants establish prayer; the plural address follows from the inclusion of descendants.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r7.anchor: ظاهره دعائي هذا المتعلق بجعلي وجعل بعض ذريتي مقيمي الصلاة ولذلك جيء بضمير الجماعة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r8.claim: A second view takes duʿāʾ to mean worship, but al-Ālūsī objects that ‘accept our worship’ would more fittingly use the plural duʿāʾunā.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r8.anchor: تعقب بأن الأنسب أن يقال فيه دعاءنا حينئذ

ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r9.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة وهبيرة عن حفص
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r9.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza, and Ḥafṣ through Hubayra read duʿāʾī with a silent yāʾ in connected speech; al-Bazzī transmits a yāʾ both connected and paused, while Qunbul hints at it when connected but pauses on alif.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p243/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة وهبيرة عن حفص ( دعائي ) بياء ساكنة في الوصل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p358/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p358/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p358/r1.claim: Establishing prayer means performing it with its pillars and maintaining it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p358/r1.anchor: {رب اجعلني مقيم الصلاة} يعني: ممن يقيم الصلاة بأركانها ويحافظ عليها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p358/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p358/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p358/r2.claim: He asks God to make some descendants people who establish prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p358/r2.anchor: {ومن ذريتي} يعني: اجعل من ذريتي من يقيمون الصلاة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p358/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p358/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p358/r3.claim: One explanation takes the prayer as deeds and worship; worship is called supplication.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p358/r3.anchor: {ربنا وتقبل دعاء} أي: عملي وعبادتي، سمى العبادة دعاء،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p358/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p358/r4.speaker: الحديث
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p358/r4.claim: Baghawī cites a hadith saying supplication is the marrow of worship.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p358/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p358/r5.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p358/r5.claim: An alternative explanation is: answer my supplication.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:40/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:40/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:40/r1.claim: Abraham asks to perform prayer properly and regularly.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:40/r1.anchor: { رب اجعلنى مقيم الصلوة } معدلا لها مواظبا عليها.

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:40/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:40/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:40/r2.claim: The phrase coordinates with the object of make me and is partitive, because revelation or past peoples show that some descendants will be unbelievers.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:40/r2.anchor: عطف على المنصوب في { اجعلنى } ، والتبعيض لعلمه بإعلام الله أو استقراء عادته

BAYDAWI-FULL:14:40/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:40/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:40/r3.claim: Accept my supplication means either answer my prayer or accept my worship.
BAYDAWI-FULL:14:40/r3.anchor: { ربنا وتقبل دعاء } واستجب دعائي أو وتقبل عبادتي

BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r9.claim: After praising God for answering prayer, Ibrāhīm asks for the worship he had set as the purpose of settling his descendants; establishing prayer is difficult for the soul without God's help.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r9.anchor: في إتباعه الدعاء بالتحلي بحلية العبادة التي أخبر أنها قصده بإسكانه من ذريته قم إقامتها

BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r10.claim: Ibrāhīm includes some of his descendants with good manners toward God, since God had informed him that some offspring would disbelieve.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r10.anchor: أعلمه بأنه يكون من ذريته من يكفر فقال أدبا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r11.claim: Prayer is the greatest pillar after faith; Ibrāhīm singles it out and uses the singular form while appealing to God through blessings uniquely bestowed on him in his time.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r11.anchor: أعظم الأركان بعد الإيمان , أفراد الضمير للدعاء بها متملقا لله تعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r12.claim: The plural address considers the descendants who follow Ibrāhīm in establishing prayer; he asks God to accept all his prayer, as if he were eager and enamored of it.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p192/r12.anchor: وجمع الضمير المضاف إليه بالنظر إلى من تبعه من ذريته لأن ما بعده كلام آخر

DURR-FULL:v5p48/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p48/r9.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v5p48/r9.claim: Ibn Jurayj says some of Abraham’s descendants will remain upon the natural faith, worshipping God until the Hour.
DURR-FULL:v5p48/r9.anchor: عن ابن جريج رضي الله عنه في قوله: {رب اجعلني مقيم الصلاة ومن ذريتي} قال: فلن يزال من ذرية إبراهيم عليه السلام ناس على الفطرة

BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r10.claim: Muqīm may mean straightening prayer, keeping it flourishing like a market, or performing it.
BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r10.anchor: معدلا لها من أقمت العود إذا قومته

BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r11.claim: The active participle rather than a verb meaning I establish signals continuity and persistence.
BURSEVI:v4p284#2/r11.anchor: والاستمرار يستفاد من العدول من الفعل إلى الاسم حيث لم يقل اجعلني أقيم الصلاة

BURSEVI:v4p285/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p285/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p285/r1.claim: From my descendants means some of them, since Abraham knew unbelievers would occur among descendants; this qualifies the lasting word in his progeny (43:28).
BURSEVI:v4p285/r1.anchor: ومن ذريتي أي وبعض ذريتي عطف على المنصوب في اجعلني وإنما بعض

BURSEVI:v4p285/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p285/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p285/r2.claim: Ishārī, establishing prayer signifies continuing ascent, since prayer is the believer’s miʿrāj, an enduring journey in and through God.
BURSEVI:v4p285/r2.anchor: والإشارة إلى إقامة الصلاة إلى إدامة العروج فإن الصلاة معراج المؤمن

BURSEVI:v4p285/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p285/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p285/r3.claim: Abraham asks God to accept his prayer that he and some descendants establish prayer, remain firm in it, and avoid idol worship; he uses the plural because the request includes them.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r1.claim: The clause begins a new sentence but continues Abraham's prayer.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r2.claim: Here ajʿalnī means bring me into that state in the future: make me one who keeps up prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r2.anchor: وفعل { اجعلني } مستعمل في التكوين ، كما تقدم آنفا ، أي اجعلني في المستقبل مقيم الصلاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r3.claim: Iqāma here means continuance or steadfast maintenance, a usage discussed at the beginning of al-Baqara.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r3.anchor: والإقامة : الإدامة ، وتقدم في صدر سورة البقرة .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r4.claim: The phrase is an adjective to an omitted noun coordinated with the first-person suffix: make prayer-maintainers among my descendants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r4.anchor: { ومن ذريتي } صفة لموصوف محذوف معطوف على ياء المتكلم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r5.claim: Min is most plausibly initial, not partitive, since Abraham asks the fullest good for himself and his descendants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r5.anchor: لأن إبراهيم عليه السلام لا يسأل الله إلا أكمل ما يحبه لنفسه ولذريته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r6.claim: A possible partitive reading assumes God had informed Abraham that only some descendants would pray and others disbelieve; Ibn ʿĀshūr calls it weak because the prayer would then seek an accomplished result.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون { من } للتبعيض بناء على أن الله أعلمه بأن يكون من ذريته فريق يقيمون الصلاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r7.claim: Asking God to accept the prayer is a further act of humble pleading after the preceding supplications.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r7.anchor: ودعاؤه بتقبل دعائه ضراعة بعد ضراعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r8.claim: Most readers omit the final yāʾ in duʿāʾi for lightness; Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and Ḥamza retain it quiescent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p244/r8.anchor: وحذفت ياء المتكلم في دعاء } في قراءة الجمهور تخفيفا كما تقدم في قوله تعالى :

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r5.claim: Since Abraham already persevered in prayer, asking to remain established in it means asking for its continuation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r5.anchor: دعا إبراهيم عليه السلام في أمر كان مثابرا عليه متمسكا به، ومتى دعا الإنسان في مثل هذا فإنما القصد إدامة ذلك الأمر واستمراره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r6.speaker: طلحة والأعمش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r6.claim: Ṭalḥa and al-Aʿmash read duʿāʾ without a final yāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ طلحة والأعمش «دعا ربنا» بغير ياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن كثير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr pronounce a silent yāʾ in duʿāʾī when connected; some retain it only in connection and omit it at pause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وابن كثير «دعائي» بياء ساكنة في الوصل، وأثبتها بعضهم دون الوقف في الوصل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r8.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r8.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī omit the yāʾ both in connection and pause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي بغير ياء في وصل ولا وقف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r9.speaker: ورش عن نافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r9.claim: Warsh from Nāfiʿ retains the yāʾ when connecting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p342#2/r9.anchor: وروى ورش عن نافع: إثبات الياء في الوصل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p514/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p514/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p514/r3.claim: Abraham asks to be constant in prayer and uphold its limits, and asks that his descendants do likewise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p514/r3.anchor: أي: محافظا عليها مقيما لحدودها {ومن ذريتي} أي: واجعلهم كذلك مقيمين (3) الصلاة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p514/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p514/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p514/r4.claim: “Accept my supplication” means accept everything Abraham has asked for.

JISHUMI:v5p3884/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r6.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r6.claim: Al-Asamm reports a reading 'for my children,' referring to Ishmael and Isaac, but rejects it as impermissible because it contradicts the widespread reading.
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r6.anchor: وحكى الأصم عن بعضهم ولولدي بغير ألف يعني: إسماعيل وإسحاق

JISHUMI:v5p3884/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3884/r14.claim: Acceptance (taqabbul) includes the granting of recompense.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p527/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p527/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p527/r1.claim: “And some of my descendants” coordinates with the object of “make me”; Abraham asks for only some because God disclosed that some descendants would be unbelievers, as in 2:124.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p527/r1.anchor: وبعض ذريتي ، عطفا على المنصوب في اجعلني ، وإنما بعض لأنه علم بإعلام الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p527/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p527/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p527/r2.claim: “Accept my prayer” means accept my worship.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p527/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p527/r12.speaker: مجاهد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p527/r12.claim: Mujahid says God answered Abraham: none of his descendants worshipped an idol after the prayer, the land became safe and fruitful, Abraham became an imam, some descendants established prayer, and God showed him the rites and accepted his repentance.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p527/r12.anchor: وعن مجاهد : قد استجاب الله له فيما سأل ، فلم يعبد أحد من ولده صنما بعد دعوته ، وجعل البلد آمنا

MUQATIL:14:40-41/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:40-41/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:40-41/r1.claim: Ibrahim asks that his descendants also establish prayer.

MUQATIL:14:40-41/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:14:40-41/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:14:40-41/r2.claim: He asks God to answer his prayer that he and his descendants establish prayer.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#4/r1.claim: Abraham asks for some of his descendants to establish prayer, since God had informed him that unbelievers would occur among them.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#4/r1.anchor: وبعض ذريتى عطفا على المنصوب في اجعلنى وإنما بعض لانه علم باعلام الله أنه يكون في ذريته كفار

NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#4/r2.speaker: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#4/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that people of Abraham's descendants will remain upon the natural faith until the Hour.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#4/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما لا يزال من ولد إبراهيم ناس على الفطرة إلى ان تقوم الساعة

NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#4/r3.claim: Makkī retains yāʾ in duʿāʾ at pause and connection; Abū ʿAmr and Ḥamza retain it in connection, while the others omit it.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#4/r3.anchor: بالياء في الوصل والوقف مكى وافقه أبو عمرو وحمزة في الوصل الباقون بلاياء

NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p233#4/r4.claim: The request means either answer my prayer or accept my worship.

QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r9.claim: Abraham asks to be among those steadfast in Islam and adherence to its rulings.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r9.anchor: أي من الثابتين على الإسلام والتزام أحكامه

QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r10.claim: He asks God to make some of his descendants people who establish prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r10.anchor: أي واجعل من ذريتي من يقيمها

QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:14:38-41/r11.claim: “Accept my supplication” means accept my worship; the commentator links it to the call to pray in 40:60 and cites the saying that supplication is the marrow of worship.

QASHANI:14:39-41/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:14:39-41/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:14:39-41/r3.claim: The prayer is to make the speaker maintain the prayer of witnessing, and to make each descendant maintain a prayer appropriate to them.
QASHANI:14:39-41/r3.anchor: صلاة الشهود { ومن ذريتي } كلا منهم مقيم صلاة تخصه

QASHANI:14:39-41/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:14:39-41/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:14:39-41/r4.claim: Accepting the prayer means accepting the request for complete annihilation in God.

RAZI-FULL:v19p110/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p110/r2.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v19p110/r2.claim: His associates also infer from Abraham's request to establish prayer that God alone brings commanded acts about; Abraham thus affirmed that all acts are from God.
RAZI-FULL:v19p110/r2.anchor: وقوله : { رب اجعلنى مقيم الصلواة ومن ذريتى } يدل على أن فعل المأمورات لا يحصل إلا من الله

RAZI-FULL:v19p110/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p110/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p110/r3.claim: The preposition min is partitive: Abraham asks that some of his descendants be established in prayer, since God had informed him that some descendants would be unbelievers.
RAZI-FULL:v19p110/r3.anchor: كلمة ( من ) في قوله : { ومن ذريتى } للتبعيض ، وإنما ذكر هذا التبعيض

RAZI-FULL:v19p110/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p110/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v19p110/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas takes duʿāʾ here to mean worship, citing Abraham's statement that he would leave those whom his people worshipped besides God.
RAZI-FULL:v19p110/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : يريد عبادتي بدليل قوله تعالى : { وأعتزلكم وما تدعون من دون الله }

QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r10.claim: ‘Make me one who establishes prayer’ implies that human acts are created: making prayer for him means creating prayer for him.
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r10.anchor: إشارة إلى أن أفعال العباد مخلوقة ، فمعناه اجعل صلاتي

QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r11.claim: Abraham asks God to make some of his descendants people who pray.

QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r12.claim: The qualification that some descendants pray is consistent with the statement that God’s covenant does not reach wrongdoers.
QUSHAYRI:v2p127/r12.anchor: لأنه أخبره في موضع آخر بقوله : لا ينال عهدي الظالمين

STUDYQURAN:14:40/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:40/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:40/r1.claim: A performer of prayer may mean someone firm in religion.
STUDYQURAN:14:40/r1.anchor: A performer of prayer can refer to one who is firm in religion

STUDYQURAN:14:40/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:40/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:40/r2.claim: Alternatively, it may mean someone persistent in the actual practice of prayer.
STUDYQURAN:14:40/r2.anchor: or to one who is persistent in the actual act of prayer

STUDYQURAN:14:40/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:40/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:40/r3.claim: Abraham may be asking God to accept his worship in general.
STUDYQURAN:14:40/r3.anchor: may be a request on the part of Abraham that God accept his worship in general

STUDYQURAN:14:40/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:14:40/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:14:40/r4.claim: Alternatively, Abraham may ask God to accept the supplication made in this verse in particular.
STUDYQURAN:14:40/r4.anchor: or his supplication as mentioned in this verse in particular

TAB-FULL:v13p702#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p702#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p702#2/r1.claim: Abraham asks to perform the prayer God obligated him to perform, and asks that some of his descendants also establish prayer as part of worshipful obedience.
TAB-FULL:v13p702#2/r1.anchor: وعبادتي إياك، وهذا نظير الخبر الذي روي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v13p702#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p702#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p702#2/r2.claim: He asks God to accept his deeds and worship.
TAB-FULL:v13p702#2/r2.anchor: وعبادتي إياك، وهذا نظير الخبر الذي روي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v13p702#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p702#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v13p702#2/r3.claim: The Prophet says that supplication is worship and recites 40:60.
TAB-FULL:v13p702#2/r3.anchor: عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: «إن الدعاء هو العبادة»

TABATABAI:14:39-41/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:39-41/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:39-41/r3.claim: Establishing prayer is attributable to God through permission and will, and to the servant through undertaking and action, as with asking God to keep one from idolatry.
TABATABAI:14:39-41/r3.anchor: لإقامة الصلاة نسبة إليه تعالى بالإذن والمشية كما أن لها نسبة إلى العبد بالتصدي والعمل

TABATABAI:14:39-41/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:39-41/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:39-41/r4.claim: This is Abraham’s second prayer shared with descendants; it follows the first shared request to be kept and his sons from idol worship, and is followed by a third shared prayer for forgiveness.
TABATABAI:14:39-41/r4.anchor: وهذه الفقرة ثاني دعاء يشترك فيه هو عليه السلام وذريته

TABATABAI:14:39-41/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:39-41/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:39-41/r5.claim: Abraham asks first for himself because he wants his descendants to attain and join him in excellence, as in his request for lasting good mention and in God’s making him an imam and his descendants after a trial.
TABATABAI:14:39-41/r5.anchor: وقد أفرد نفسه في جميع الفقرات الثلاث عن غيره

TABATABAI:14:39-41/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:39-41/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:39-41/r6.claim: “My sons” in the first prayer and “my descendants” here both mean some descendants, so the two requests agree.
TABATABAI:14:39-41/r6.anchor: فقد تقدم أن المراد ببنيه بعضهم لا جميعهم

TABATABAI:14:39-41/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:39-41/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:39-41/r7.claim: Asking God to accept the prayer intensifies and insists on it, just as the explanation that idols led many astray reinforces the first request.
TABATABAI:14:39-41/r7.anchor: فإن سؤال تقبل الدعاء إلحاح وإصرار وتأكيد

TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r1.claim: The repeated vocatives vary between “my Lord” and “our Lord”: requests specific to Abraham’s precedence and imamate use the singular, while shared requests use the plural.
TABATABAI:14:35-41#3/r1.anchor: النداء المكرر الذي فيه بلفظ { رب } و { ربنا } والعناية فيما أضيف

TABRISI:14:37/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37/r3.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة وهبيرة عن حفص
TABRISI:14:37/r3.claim: These readers retain the yāʾ in دعائي when continuing.
TABRISI:14:37/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحمزة وهبيرة عن حفص وتقبل دعائي ربنا بإثبات الياء في الوصل

TABRISI:14:37/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37/r4.speaker: البزي عن ابن كثير
TABRISI:14:37/r4.claim: Al-Bazzī is reported to retain the yāʾ both in connection and pause; another description says it is indicated only in connection and omitted at pause.
TABRISI:14:37/r4.anchor: وفي رواية البزي عن ابن كثير أنه يصل ويقف بياء

TABRISI:14:37/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37/r5.speaker: الباقون
TABRISI:14:37/r5.claim: The remaining readers omit the yāʾ and read دعاء.

TABRISI:14:37/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37/r14.claim: Keeping yāʾ in connection is analogical; when it is not pronounced, the kasra signals it.
TABRISI:14:37/r14.anchor: وأما من وصل دعائي بياء فهو القياس من شم الياء في الوصل

TABRISI:14:37/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37/r15.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:14:37/r15.claim: Deleting yāʾ is more analogical at pause than in connection because pause alters final letters; al-Aʿshā's lines illustrate this.
TABRISI:14:37/r15.anchor: قال أبو علي حذف الياء في الوقف أقيس من حذفها في الوصل

TABRISI:14:37#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:37#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:37#2/r1.claim: The cited al-Aʿshā lines illustrate deletion of a final yāʾ at pause.
TABRISI:14:37#2/r1.anchor: ومن شانىء كاسف وجهه إذا ما انتسبت له أنكرن

TABRISI:14:39-41/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:39-41/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:39-41/r3.claim: The second clause means make some descendants establish prayer; its verb is omitted because the preceding verb supplies it.
TABRISI:14:39-41/r3.anchor: تقديره واجعل من ذريتي مقيم الصلاة فحذف الفعل لأن ما قبله يدل عليه

TABRISI:14:39-41/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:39-41/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:39-41/r4.claim: Ibrahim asks for لطف to establish prayer and adhere to religion, and the same for a group of descendants who became Muslims.
TABRISI:14:39-41/r4.anchor: بأن يلطف له اللطف الذي عنده يقيم الصلاة ويتمسك بالدين وأن يفعل مثل ذلك بجماعة من ذريته

TABRISI:14:39-41/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:14:39-41/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:14:39-41/r5.claim: Accepting prayer means answering it; accepting an act of obedience means rewarding it.
TABRISI:14:39-41/r5.anchor: فإن قبول الدعاء إنما هو الإجابة وقبول الطاعة الإثابة

THALABI:v5p322/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p322/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p322/r13.claim: Abraham asks God to make some of his descendants people who establish prayer as well.
THALABI:v5p322/r13.anchor: رب اجعلني مقيم الصلاة ومن ذريتي أيضا واجعلهم مقيمي الصلاة

THALABI:v5p323/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p323/r1.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v5p323/r1.claim: The commentators explain duʿāʾ here as worship; the Prophet calls supplication the core of worship and Quran 40:60 names supplication worship.

THALABI:v5p323/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p323/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v5p323/r2.claim: The Prophet says supplication is the core of worship.
THALABI:v5p323/r2.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «الدعاء مخ العبادة»

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p491/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p491/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p491/r1.claim: Ibrahim asks to be a constant establisher of prayer using an adjective, which is more enduring and emphatic than asking to perform the action; al-Wahidi links this discussion to another verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p491/r1.anchor: ذكره على النعت ولم يذكره على الفعل؛ لأن النعت ألزم وأكثر من الفعل، كأنه قال: رب اجعلني

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p491/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p491/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p491/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj reads this as asking God to make some of Ibrahim's descendants people who establish prayer, like the partitive min in his earlier request and in 14:34.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p491/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج: أي: واجعل من ذريتي من يقيم الصلاة (¬4)، وهذا كما ذكرنا في قوله: {إني أسكنت من ذريتي}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p491/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p491/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p491/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says duʿa here means worship, as in the saying that supplication is the core of worship.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:39-43/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:39-43/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:39-43/r2.claim: Abraham asks God to make some of his descendants people who establish prayer.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:14:39-43/r2.anchor: { ومن ذريتي } أي: واجعل منهم من يقيم الصلاة

MAJAZ:v1p342/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p342/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p342/r2.claim: The compact phrase omits a pronoun: ‘appoint from my descendants someone who establishes prayer.’
MAJAZ:v1p342/r2.anchor: رب اجعلني مقيم الصلاة ومن ذريتي» (40) مجازه مجاز المختصر الذي فيه ضمير كقوله: واجعل من ذريتى من يقيم الصلاة.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r2.claim: The account presents Abraham's grateful devotion and supplication as an example of servitude to God, and points to salvation through his monotheistic way.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r2.anchor: Ayrıca Allah’ın verdiği sayısız ve sınırsız nimetlerin şükrünü yerine getiren bir kulun yani Hz. İbrâhim’in Allah’a karşı tutumu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r10.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r10.claim: Commentators say Abraham made the prayer in these verses after Mecca had become a settlement and he and Ishmael had built the Kaaba.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:14:35/r10.anchor: Müfessirlere göre İbrâhim bu âyetlerde bildirilen duasını da Mekke yerleşim merkezi haline geldikten ve İsmâil ile birlikte Kâbe’yi inşa ettikten sonra yapmıştır
